paras: The killing of Joe Biyard was the fatal police shooting of a dock worker on Fahm street, near Bay, on the morning of May 2, 1919, reported by the Savannah Tribune. Biyard was shot after he objected to an officer's treatment of a woman under arrest, and according to the paper a second officer then shot him three times inside a store.
Biyard was a dock worker of about 28 who came from St. Helena island. The Tribune spelled his surname "Biyard" in its text and "Binyard" in its headline.

At about 10:20 that morning, an officer on Fahm street was arresting a woman the paper described as a "Negro woman." Biyard objected to the way she was being handled, and the argument that followed ended with the officer and Biyard "coming together." In the tussle on the ground Biyard was shot, after which he ran into a nearby store. There, "it is stated," another officer shot him three times, and he died.
The coverage does not name either officer, and no report of an inquest, arrest or charge was found.

The Savannah Tribune, a Black paper, carried the shooting the next day as a short front-page item under the headline "JOE BINYARD SHOT TO DEATH YESTERDAY." The item reported the killing without editorial comment, attributing the shooting in the store to what "is stated" rather than vouching for it directly. No later report in the Tribune or other Black papers searched returned to the case.

reader.title: Killing of Joe Biyard
bases: Police officers shot Biyard to death during and after a confrontation over an arrest; no mob or crowd is reported (A1).
Only one article, the Savannah Tribune's local report of the next day, describes the shooting, and parts of its account are attributed to 'it is stated' (A1).

accounts.label: Savannah Tribune local report
accounts.gist: Biyard objected to an officer's handling of a woman under arrest, an argument led to a tussle in which he was shot, and, 'it is stated', a second officer shot him three times in a store he had run into.

framing.detail: The Savannah Tribune ran a brief front-page item headlined 'JOE BINYARD SHOT TO DEATH YESTERDAY', reporting the shooting in plain terms and hedging the store shooting with 'it is stated'.

conflicts.note: The same article spells the surname two ways; neither is confirmed by another source.
